column1: # Baseline for bin/check-throughput-regression.mjs. Tab-separated: kind, name, value, unit.
# A COMMITTED RATCHET, UPDATED BY A HUMAN. Nothing in CI writes here - there is no data branch and no
# contents: write grant, so this file is the whole baseline.
# EVERY ROW COMES FROM ONE RUN, and that is a rule rather than a coincidence. A rate from one run
# normalised by class times from another is not a comparison, it is two runs pretending to be one.
# These are from run 33487654993 - master's tree, hosted runner, all 3,000,000 records completed.
# UPDATING IT: take every row from a single `perf baseline (master)` run and say WHICH run in the
# commit, so the next reader can tell a re-baseline from a regression that got normalised away. Never
# update it to make a red lane green without saying that is what you are doing.
# The three class-seconds rows are the machine-speed reference, not measurements of anything in their
# own right. All three performance classes are listed: bin/perf-backfill.mjs's first version summed
# whatever classes happened to run and its denominator swung from 130s to 1335s across branches, which
# conflated "the subject slowed" with "the lane changed".
